contract: Concurrent numeric, borrowed host DNS or retained <=64 prepared endpoints return the same UPGRADING peer. Explicit HTTP Host/Target and mandatory TLS identity are distinct from routing. One original factory-entry HTTP setup deadline spans snapshots/owner queue/DNS/candidates/TLS/Upgrade; each RPC has its own entry clock. Snapshot bounded native TLS client metadata before return. Only the winning TCP connection starts TLS. No RPC before checked101, no replay/redirect/reconnect/credential retry or downgrade. Close joins real owned callback/raw/TLS/WS duties; host Resolver backend/code/data is joined separately.
ownership: Fresh native TLS root context and replaceable events are distinct real owners. A separate root descriptor retains the peer, then an HTTP event credit is bound after verified Open/outside driver before HTTP. The existing exact HTTP-to-WS event exchange transfers the event slot; root peer credit retires at native destruction. No private Core access, relaxed state guard, diagnostic inspection alias, invented owner or new runtime.
